findings.statement: At the pinned F2b bytes both live carriers are present: HC1 at line 152 and HC2 at line 246, each contradicted by the chain at line 239.

The live-hash F2b verdict set is split: 7 accept(s) [worker-052, worker-061, worker-071, worker-072, worker-082, worker-090, worker-16] against 32 revise(s) [worker-002, worker-007, worker-017, worker-018, worker-020, worker-028, worker-029, worker-034, worker-035, worker-038, worker-041, worker-044, worker-053, worker-061, worker-062, worker-066, worker-069, worker-072, worker-075, worker-082, worker-085, worker-088, worker-089, worker-095, worker-097] and 0 inconclusive. A reviewer may appear on both sides at different times at the same bytes (verdict flip); the census keeps each dated verdict.

7 of 7 live-hash accept instruments name neither carrier text and 7 of 7 never read the contradicted chain field; their accepts therefore cannot have discharged the HC1/HC2 revise findings at these bytes.

13 of 32 live-hash revise instruments are carrier-capable (both name a carrier text and read the chain); the blocking findings are carried by instruments that can see the carriers, not by the accept instruments.

The controller's own fresh scan (runtime/state/controller_verification/lifecycle_20260912-011029.json) counts F2b two_distinct_accepts=True with accept reviewers ['worker-071', 'worker-072', 'worker-090']: the >=2-accept coverage criterion is numerically met at the same bytes that carry both live blocking carriers. Whether those accepts discharge the revise findings is an adjudication for the audit lead.

Of the controller-counted accepts ['worker-071', 'worker-072', 'worker-090'], 0 of 3 have any resolved instrument that names a carrier text and reads the contradicted chain ([('worker-090', 'block_referencing_only'), ('worker-072', 'block_referencing_only'), ('worker-071', 'block_referencing_only')]).
